bug_semantics: Authenticated customer IDOR in shop OrderController::reorder(): the handler loaded any sales order with orderRepository->findOrFail($id) and then copied that order's items into the caller's cart, without checking that the order belonged to auth()->guard('customer')->id(). The customer-auth route shop.customers.account.orders.reorder therefore let customer A supply customer B's order id (GET /customer/account/orders/reorder/{id} after 4e248cdb) and receive B's line items. Sibling actions view/cancel/printInvoice already scoped by customer_id; only reorder omitted that check.
flaw_origin: The customer reorder feature was first added in 3e44549e65451c90bbedee03f120c5b27854aeae (Jitendra, 2024-04-08). That commit wrote Shop OrderController::reorder() using findOrFail($id) while the same file's view() already used findOneWhere(['customer_id' => auth customer, 'id' => $id]) plus abort_if 404. A next-day follow-up 4e248cdbcd7b965a12c631ba41649b8d0d67ae11 kept the same unscoped lookup, switched the route POST->GET, and redirected into the current shop cart (the advisory PoC shape). It did not first-write the IDOR line.
